vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: cellcog
Version: 2.0.6

The skill bundle describes an AI orchestration service that requires an external API key and requests broad permissions, specifically instructing the user or agent to modify the OpenClaw gateway configuration to allow 'sessions_send' and 'sessions_list' (SKILL.md). It encourages the agent to send local file contents to an external endpoint (cellcog.ai) and mentions a background daemon for WebSocket-based result delivery. While these capabilities are aligned with the stated purpose of a multi-modal research agent, the combination of security configuration changes, external data transmission, and the requirement to 'always print the entire message' (which could facilitate prompt injection from the API) represents a significant security risk.

llm.summary: The skill's requirements and instructions align with its advertised multi-modal AI purpose, but its runtime guidance allows sending arbitrary local files to an external service so users should exercise caution with sensitive data and API keys.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (multi-modal Any→Any AI) matches what the SKILL.md instructs: a Python SDK client, an API key (CELLCOG_API_KEY), and the ability to submit files and request multiple output artifacts. Requested binary (python3) and single env var are appropriate for an SDK-based service.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The instructions require embedding absolute local file paths inside <SHOW_FILE> tags so the service reads file contents — this is necessary for multi-file multimodal processing but also means the agent will read and transmit whatever local files the user includes. The doc also instructs using notify_session_key for OpenClaw session callbacks and suggests pip install cellcog if import fails. No other unrelated files, env vars, or system paths are referenced.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files; lowest install risk. The SKILL.md suggests pip installing an SDK if missing, which is expected for a Python client but is executed by the user environment, not the skill bundle.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Only CELLCOG_API_KEY is required. This is proportional and expected for an external API service; no additional unrelated credentials or secret-like env vars are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No always:true flag, no claims to modify agent/system config, and the default ability for autonomous invocation is unchanged. The skill does reference OpenClaw gateway settings (sessions_send) but does not request persistent privileges itself.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a Python SDK wrapper to send files and prompts to the CellCog service. Before installing/using, (1) only provide files you are comfortable uploading — the <SHOW_FILE> mechanism will transmit file contents to cellcog.ai, (2) treat CELLCOG_API_KEY like a secret and only use a key tied to an account you trust, (3) confirm OpenClaw gateway 'sessions_send' behavior and who can receive notifications, and (4) review CellCog's privacy/billing docs because uploads may include sensitive data and processing can consume credits. If you need guarantees about data residency or retention, contact the service before sending sensitive material.
